topics.title: Alimony Payments and Moody Blues Album Release
topics.summary: Graham Edge discusses computerized music production for the upcoming Moody Blues album, ‘Sulemer’ (French for 'on the horse'), while recounting his alimony payments to a former wife involving Terence Stamp and managing child support. The conversation also touches on computerizing drum patterns and difficulties with complex musical sequencing.

topics.title: Stern’s London Gathering
topics.summary: Howard Stern hosts a chaotic gathering in London with Jack Bruce and Noel Redding of Cream alongside Zach Stark and Leslie on the phone. Discussions range from musical heroes to personal crises including Jack’s uncertain future, while equipment malfunctions and an attempt to form a new band add to the confusion.

topics.title: Jack Bruce Discusses Cream's Breakup and Financial Issues
topics.summary: During an extended conversation, Jack Bruce discusses his feelings about Cream’s breakup due to the band’s intense touring schedule and frustration over not receiving royalties from their albums. He recounts humorous anecdotes involving Robert Stigwood and attempts to secure financial compensation while also expressing concerns regarding lack of payment for songwriting.

topics.title: Musical Performance and Personal Discussions
topics.summary: The broadcast features a lengthy performance of the song "When The Wagons Leave," followed by discussions among participants about personal experiences, including relationships with women, past sexual encounters (described in detail), financial matters, and reflections on musicians like Jimi Hendrix and Stevie Wonder. Several speakers discuss their careers and offer opinions regarding money.

topics.title: Stievi Threatens Outburst Over Hair
topics.summary: During a radio segment, one participant expresses extreme anger over his hair after hearing about it from Stevie. Others discuss Jack’s departure and attempt an impromptu supergroup with Zach on drums.

topics.title: Jack Bruce Demands Royalties – Chaotic Phone Call
topics.summary: During an extended and confusing phone call involving multiple individuals and record label representatives, Jack Bruce repeatedly demands payment for royalties owed to him by Robert Stigwood. The conversation is marked by misinterpretations of the RSO organization, Alan Parsons' engineering work, and numerous attempts to secure financial compensation amidst considerable confusion.
